exact_items: Concern categories: wiring, workflow, state_contract, gui_alignment, design_architecture, quality, evidence_gap, corroboration, recovery, account_usage_pressure, projection_trust
severity should stay independent from blocking semantics: severity answers how bad is it; blocking_effect answers what does it prevent
Concern lifecycle: active, acknowledged, resolved, dismissed
acknowledged: user/operator has seen and accepted the concern as still real but not requiring immediate noise
dismissed: concern presentation was intentionally hidden/rejected; should require rationale when it disagrees with corroborated/high-severity evidence
resolved: underlying truth changed; should record resolution_kind
resolution_kind values: fixed, accepted_risk, superseded, merged, split, invalidated, obsoleted_by_patch, obsoleted_by_recovery
same issue persists with more evidence: update existing concern, append sources/evidence, allow severity/attention escalation
one concern was too broad: split into child concerns with lineage links
two concerns are actually the same issue: merge into one retained concern id; close/redirect the merged-away ids explicitly
older framing replaced by better/newer concern: mark older concern as resolved with resolution_kind = superseded or use explicit supersession linkage
review finding: may nominate a concern or attach evidence to an existing concern
corroboration outcome: may confirm/deny/escalate/downgrade concern credibility; should be able to turn a nominated concern into an accepted canonical concern
graph patch: may resolve a concern; may supersede a concern with successor concerns if the patch reframes the issue
recovery: may resolve operational concerns; may create follow-on concerns if restore/recovery exposes deeper integrity issues
concern owner kinds: Runtime, Package Overseer, Seam Overseer, Corroboration, Graph Patch, Recovery, User, External Resource
Add a canonical concern record family and corresponding projection contract
Add explicit concern lineage fields for merge/split/supersession
Add resolution_kind and rationale requirements for dismiss/resolve paths
Define how nominated findings become canonical concerns
Define concern-to-review/corroboration/patch/recovery linkage explicitly
classify actions by both confirmation level and reversibility
Confirmation levels: none, light, strong, hard_gate
Reversibility classes: immediate_undo, compensating_action_only, non_reversible
hard_gate: actions that must go through a canonical approval/blocked flow and cannot be bypassed by generic UI confirmation
none: safe navigation/focus actions, low-risk presentation, no user-data or live-runtime mutation
light: moderate-impact actions where accidental activation is plausible; short confirm or inline affordance
strong: actions that may discard local state, remove artifacts/worktrees, revoke accepted state, or materially change live execution; should show scope and consequence clearly
hard_gate: examples include HITL approvals, graph patch application when it changes canonical graph generation, remote-side-effect actions with explicit non-bypassable policy
do not over-promise undo when the system really only supports compensating actions
Undo only when true immediate undo exists; Reopen, Restore, Retry from Safe Point, Create New Lane, Re-request Promotion, Reapply for distinct compensating cases
strong confirmations should show: action name, target object(s), concrete consequence summary, whether local work/artifacts/history remain, reversibility class
hard_gate should show: runtime-defined allowed actions, why the gate exists, exact consequence of each allowed action, no hidden alternative path
canonical_replacement_hints: Undo / Reopen / Restore / Retry from Safe Point / Create New Lane / Re-request Promotion / Reapply
